name: Clause drafts

namesake.text: undocumented (descriptive name; the repo states no namesake)

role: Splits each held order text into numbered operative clauses and saves them as a machine-made draft inventory that a person must still check.
inputs: held order texts (Federal Register, American Presidency Project copies, Opus release zip)
outputs: texts set aside for identity doubt (IDENTITY_QUARANTINE.csv)

results.text: Found that 76 drafts of transcribed pages drop the order's final date line when the date is irregular (for example "June 30 1934."), so a whole-text quotation fails the checker for those orders. At the pinned commit the date pattern still requires a comma, so no fix is recorded.

Output of run 40056070366: 9,919 of 14,972 orders had candidate text; 9,761 drafts written (6,659 segmented "good", 3,102 "partial"), 70,615 clauses; 149 orders not segmented, 9 held back for identity doubt. 4,964 drafts rest on American Presidency Project transcriptions.

history.text: Added American Presidency Project pages as a fallback input, labelled transcription-based.
Hooked into the readiness tracker with the other first machine jobs.
Job added ("job 3").

caveats: "Good" means only that the automatic structure checks found no problem, never that the law was read.
Clause boundaries, kinds and target orders are machine guesses; legal fields are left empty.
Does not prove a saved copy is authentic and never changes a status or count.

name: Claim drafts

namesake.text: undocumented (descriptive name; the repo states no namesake)

role: Pre-fills one draft whole-lifecycle claim for every order that has a provisional status, and lists exactly what a research agent still has to decide.

results.text: Output of the scheduled run finished 2026-10-29T07:08:32Z: 3,403 drafts, all for decided orders; 1,145 have only judgment fields left (210 yes, 935 no); 434 orders carry at least one conflict. None of the 3,403 machine search records is filled in as a claim field.
Pilot use: Mansfield drew its pool from the "only judgment left" rows of the to-do list; the label hid missing, truncated or misassociated evidence in several orders.

history.text: Reads the Namier person-name leads when drafting.
Made the embedded claim checker offline-only; before this it inherited a 400-download allowance despite promising no network use.
Wired in the printed-volume jobs (OFR compilations, Richardson, OFR 1989 Codification).
Job added ("job 8").

caveats: Drafts are not accepted lifecycle claims; a draft committed unchanged turns on no readiness step except the original-text step.
Every judgment field (state, first end, savings, rationale) is left empty on purpose.
The claim-checker verdict in the to-do list covers only copied sources and quotations, never that the claim passes.

name: Claim kit and case bundles

namesake.text: undocumented (descriptive name; the repo states no namesake)

role: Freezes one evidence dossier and one blank decision sheet per order, then turns an agent's reviewed decision sheet into a full claim; case-bundles packs each dossier into a single startup file.
inputs: held texts declared by source jobs
outputs: assembled claims after an agent decides

results.text: Output of run 40987576100 (finished 2026-10-30T02:17:03Z): 3,403 dossiers for decided orders; 14,884 of 14,972 orders with held text; 41,564 distinct held text artifacts; 280 texts refused as the order's own text by the identity gate; 11,569 status leads for undecided identities; 0 claims assembled by the build itself.
Case-bundles run: 3,403 packets, each under the 30,000-byte cap (largest 29,894); median startup fetches per order 10 before, 1 after. The catalog records an earlier historical benchmark of 9 to 1.
Same-input machine path on a real batch: 214.0 s with the earlier code, 53.5 s repaired, identical claims; the report states this is not evidence of a model-token saving.
Matched A/B of compact packets against ordinary preparation: producer time fell 33% but total input tokens rose 21.8% and elapsed time 5.4%; one proposal upheld per arm.
First 50-order claim-kit pilot in expected-easy families: 12 accepted, 38 unable, first-pass rejection 16.7%, no cost reduction.

history.text: Planted-control reviews are bound to the seeded task scope; a probe-scope review no longer earns control credit.
PR104 repairs: request-scoped Valla context, one verified fragment index per run; a real completion went from 506 s and 0 filed to 122 s and 16 filed on identical pinned inputs.

Original-selection fix: tiered ranking plus an identity gate; 69 of 14,886 orders with held text change their original, 8 of them among decided dossiers. A grade bug had labelled 1,824 of 3,403 dossiers' transcriptions "derivative_lead".
Number citations without a change verb now make the citing order a known actor (known pairs 16,626 to 17,763 in the local rebuild).
Offline whole-corpus claim kit built.

caveats: Nothing here chooses or changes legal status; every legal field needs an agent's approval and a separate reviewer.
Dossiers hold only what is held; 280 texts were refused as order text and an unheld source stays a gap.
Packaging benefits are real for startup fetches but the matched test did not show a total token saving.
Claim-kit runs after Valla (jobs/claim-kit/after.txt); Valla reads canonical claims and reviews, not kit output, so there is no cycle.

name: X1 class engine

namesake.text: none given beyond the catalog label "first of the excavator series"

results.text: Run output: 8,014 pre-1937 orders typed (land 3,028; spent 2,153; standing 1,878; swept 861; unknown 94); the summary states it is lead-only.

Pilot: only 52 of 8,014 had both a provisional status and a held text; 6 submitted, 5 upheld by an independent AI reviewer, 1 rejected, 46 blocked. On the branch run the tracker counted the 5 as ready (130 to 135).
Fresh holdout of 80 orders: exact type 90% (95% CI 82-95%), class 95%; 42 of the 80 labels used the same WPA summaries the classifier reads, so that part is agreement, not independent validation.
22 type rules approved only as lead patterns after four rounds of independent AI review; 656 texts in 132 clusters; 128 sheets.

history.text: Event sources are now read from every job's published source records; a run published 8 of 8 held event sources with phrases found (before, 7 of 8 showed pending).
Production-line audit found X1 omits five held passing texts; repair proposed in an unmerged stack.
Type rules rewritten in round 2 after independent review.
First build: classifier, rules, event register, clusterer, sheets.

caveats: Every output is a lead; no type, rule or sheet decides an order or touches the human-certified count (0).
The report's 463 hours saved is a model recalibration, not measured labor (tool-tier audit).
Direct production was modest: five claims from 52 attempted, the rest blocked by missing evidence.
The risk-tiered (20% audit) review path is off by default; the owner has not approved it.

name: Cruden retrieval cache

namesake.text: Alexander Cruden, whose 1737 concordance listed every occurrence of every word of the Bible

role: Looks up, for each order in a research packet, every held text that cites its number or code name, and now caches the search features so repeat lookups are faster.
outputs: companion file with source hashes and coverage

results.text: Matched seven-order run on the integrated generation: 90.903 s legacy, 13.989 s cold cache, 8.847 s warm; JSON and Markdown outputs identical; more bytes are read; not an end-to-end research saving.
Earlier profile on the PR108 branch: 71.010 s original, 11.569 s cold, 5.541 s warm; exact output across four packets; 11 focused tests and 61 independent overlapping checks pass.

Native producer assignment (EO 10673, EO 10772): 2 query runs over 33,118 readable texts, 19 full hit-source reads, legacy output byte-identical; documented a duplicate-path self-hit, neighboring-regulation signals and an OCR suffix miss.
Before the cache, a seven-order lookup was the largest remaining machine cost in the PR104 rehearsal (113.6 s).

history.text: Source-bound feature cache added (PR108); legacy matching and the old search command are kept.
Created in the NIRA sweep so producers stop rebuilding search scripts.

caveats: Producer-operated script that reads a prepared packet folder; not a jobs/ runner dependency.
A match is a lead, and no match is evidence of absence; nothing about authenticity, identity or legal effect follows.
The cache is disposable and checked against source bytes; it is not a custody record.
In the NIRA sweep, batches using Cruden cost less but the saving was not attributed to the tool.
